target_capability: DFlash2 verified-row counters and net-cost comparison
assertions: The response routes to qualification and distinguishes produced, verified, accepted and retained rows.
The response explains that draft_n counts verified proposals rather than all produced proposals, and that accepted tokens per cycle do not prove net speed or quality.
The response identifies auto versus all verify-row policy as a changed control, including timing/history dependence and possible greedy or seeded output variation.
The response explains that API intervals exclude initial admission and the decode rate excludes the first emission, so client E2E latency and complete task quality are still required.
The response requires same target/draft and prepared-byte identities, hardware/power/cache/concurrency/precision controls and frozen quality/performance gates before comparison.
The response uses or references bundled summarize_rounds.py for descriptive ABBA samples without inventing a PASS threshold, executing an engine or claiming reproduction.
The response distinguishes model-stop/output-limit exclusions from later stop-string truncation, whose accepted proposals still count; it does not recompute acceptance from visible output alone.
